about.title: Simi Valley Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Most of what fills a Simi Valley home or garage was made somewhere else and passed through several hands before it reached you. When one of those items fails — a space heater that ignites, a ladder rung that snaps, a car part that gives out on SR-118 — the question is rarely whether you did something wrong. Under California's strict liability rules, the focus stays on the product: was it defectively designed, badly manufactured, or sold without a proper warning, and did that defect cause your injury? You generally do not have to prove the company was careless. That distinction matters in Ventura County courtrooms, and it matters to the manufacturer, distributor, and retailer who may each share responsibility. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that puts injured Simi Valley residents in touch with an independent attorney who handles defective product claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Hold onto the product, the packaging, and any receipts. The item itself is often your strongest evidence.

whyChoose.title: Why Simi Valley Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict liability, explained plainly
items.desc: In California you usually need to show the product was defective and that the defect hurt you — not that anyone was negligent. The attorneys in our network understand how to frame a design, manufacturing, or warning defect under that standard.

items.title: Every link in the chain is examined
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the retailer where you bought the item may each be responsible. An independent attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim rather than letting one company point at another.

items.title: Evidence preservation from day one
items.desc: The product itself is central to these cases, and it can be lost or altered quickly. A connected attorney can help you secure the item, its packaging, and purchase records before they disappear.

items.question: My airbag never deployed in a crash on Los Angeles Avenue. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It may be both. Simi Valley recorded 357 injury collisions in 2025, and in some of those crashes the other driver is not the only party worth looking at. If a safety component failed to work as designed, the vehicle or parts manufacturer could face a strict liability claim alongside any claim against the driver. An attorney can evaluate whether the failure points to a defect.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was faulty?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often runs on strict liability, meaning the question is whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect that caused your injury. The maker's state of mind is usually not something you need to establish. That said, each case turns on its facts, and an attorney can tell you how the rule applies to yours.

items.question: I already threw the broken product away. Can I still do anything?
items.answer: Do not assume the claim is gone, but act quickly. Check whether the item is still in your trash, storage, or with a repair shop, and gather photos, receipts, the model number, and any recall notices. Keeping the product is strongly preferred because it is often the key piece of evidence, so if you still have it, set it aside untouched.
